title: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Diagnosis and Metabolic Screening

evidenceAudit.scope: Woman or adolescent girl in a Saudi primary care or gynaecology clinic with irregular cycles, hirsutism, acne, hair loss or infertility: apply the 2023 international diagnostic criteria, exclude other causes, screen glucose, blood pressure, lipids, sleep apnoea, mood and endometrial risk, give lifestyle advice, and choose first medicines for cycle control, hirsutism and ovulation. Uses the 2023 international guideline, two Saudi survey studies and the product labels.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-14.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national guideline on polycystic ovary syndrome was found. The 2023 international evidence-based guideline (Monash University, endorsed by many societies) is used; its evidence is described by the authors as low to moderate quality.

Saudi data used: an Eastern Province online survey of 408 women (symptom-based prevalence 19.9%, 16.7% with formal diagnosis) and a national online survey of 1,182 diagnosed women (28.6% waited six months or more after seeking care; only 42.7% had adequate information). Both are self-reported online surveys.

Every medicine here is off-label for polycystic ovary syndrome: metformin, drospirenone with ethinyl estradiol (Yasmin), spironolactone and letrozole labels cover other indications, so the dose and instructions come from the label while the use comes from the guideline.

Letrozole for ovulation induction: the label gives 2.5 mg once daily for its breast cancer indications only; the cycle days, dose escalation and monitoring schedule for ovulation induction were not found in a source read, so they are left to the fertility specialist's protocol.

The guideline does not recommend one specific contraceptive pill; Yasmin is written as the product whose label was read, and it has drospirenone with anti-mineralocorticoid activity, so another low-dose pill may suit a woman better. Which brands are available in Saudi Arabia was not checked.

The ultrasound and anti-Müllerian hormone cut-offs for polycystic ovarian morphology were not read in full; only the follicle number, ovarian volume of 10 mL or more and 'population and assay-specific cut-offs' statements were used.
Saudi-validated hirsutism scoring (modified Ferriman-Gallwey cut-off of 4 to 6 depends on ethnicity) and local vitamin D, insulin resistance and obesity thresholds were not found.
Semaglutide, liraglutide and orlistat are mentioned by the guideline for weight in adults with the condition but no labels were reviewed, so no regimen is written for them.
Figures were read by automated extraction of web and label text; spot-check each figure and dose against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: Polycystic ovary syndrome is the commonest endocrine disorder of reproductive-age women, with a prevalence of 10% to 13% by the Rotterdam criteria (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.6.1). Diagnosis in adults needs two of three features: clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, and polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound or a raised anti-Müllerian hormone (International PCOS guideline 2023, Section Summary of key recommendations). Women with the condition have an increased risk of impaired glucose tolerance and type 2 diabetes at any age and body mass index (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.9.1). Insulin resistance is part of the pathophysiology, but routine insulin assays are not recommended (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.9.12). Obstructive sleep apnoea, depression, anxiety and eating disorders are more common (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.10.1 and Recommendation 2.2.1). Pregnancy risks are higher: gestational diabetes, hypertension, pre-eclampsia, preterm birth (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.10.2).

symptoms: Irregular or infrequent periods (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.1.1).
Excess facial or body hair, acne or female-pattern hair loss (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.3.3).
Difficulty conceiving because of absent ovulation (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 5.3.1).
Weight gain, low mood, anxiety or snoring with unrefreshing sleep (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 2.2.1 and Recommendation 1.10.2).
physicalSigns: Hirsutism: a modified Ferriman-Gallwey score of 4 to 6 or more, depending on ethnicity (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.3.5).
Acne or female-pattern hair loss, which alone are weak predictors of raised androgens (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.3.2).
Higher weight, central adiposity and raised blood pressure (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.10.6).
Ovarian volume of 10 mL or more, or 10 or more follicles per section on transabdominal ultrasound (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.4.8).
redFlags: Rapid onset of severe hirsutism or virilisation, or markedly raised androgens: look for an ovarian or adrenal tumour, congenital adrenal hyperplasia or Cushing syndrome (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.2.9).
New or worsening hyperandrogenism after menopause: rule out androgen-secreting tumour or ovarian hyperthecosis (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.7.4).
Primary amenorrhoea by age 15, or more than 3 years after breast development: assess urgently (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.1.1).
Persistent heavy or prolonged bleeding or amenorrhoea over long periods: consider endometrial hyperplasia (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.11.2).
Moderate to severe depression or any suicidal thoughts: urgent mental health assessment (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 2.2.1).
Possible pregnancy before starting letrozole or an anti-androgen: do a pregnancy test (Letrozole label, Section Contraindications; International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.6.3).
precipitants: Higher weight and weight gain, especially in adolescence (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.1.4).
Family history of diabetes in the woman or first-degree relatives (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.9.7).
Existing diabetes, which increases the chance of the condition (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.9.8).

differentials.condition: Thyroid disease, hyperprolactinaemia or non-classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Other causes of irregular cycles and hyperandrogenism are excluded before the diagnosis (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.2.9).
Rapid onset, marked androgen excess or virilisation (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.2.9).
Other Cushingoid features with hyperandrogenism (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.2.9).
Irregular cycles are normal in the first year after menarche; assess later (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.1.1).
Iatrogenic causes of androgen excess (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.2.9).

ruleIn.testName: Total and free testosterone (free androgen index)
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Raised total or free testosterone or free androgen index
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Use total and free testosterone, measured by tandem mass spectrometry where possible; off the combined pill for at least 3 months if it must be measured (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.2.1 and Recommendation 1.2.6).
ruleIn.normalValue: Total and free testosterone within the adult female reference range of the reporting laboratory

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Use either anti-Müllerian hormone or ultrasound, not both, and never as a single test (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.5.1, Recommendation 1.5.3 and Recommendation 1.5.5).
ruleIn.normalValue: Below the assay- and population-specific cut-off of the laboratory

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Look for polycystic ovarian morphology in adults when needed for the diagnosis
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Follicle number per ovary above the current threshold, or ovarian volume of 10 mL or more
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Follicle number per ovary is the best marker; transabdominal scans report ovarian volume 10 mL or more or 10 or more follicles per section (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.4.1, Recommendation 1.4.7 and Recommendation 1.4.8).

ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Most accurate test; fasting glucose or HbA1c can be used if it cannot be done, with less accuracy (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.9.9 and Recommendation 1.9.10).
ruleOut.normalValue: Fasting and 2-hour glucose within the normal range of the reporting laboratory

clinicalManagement.title: Suspect and take the history
actions: Ask about cycle length, hirsutism, acne, hair loss, weight change, fertility plans, mood, sleep and family history of diabetes (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.3.3).
Examine hair growth with the modified Ferriman-Gallwey score, blood pressure and body mass index (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.3.5).
In adolescents, discuss the value and timing of diagnosis with the girl and her parents or guardian (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.1.3).

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm the diagnosis
actions: Check for two of three criteria after excluding other causes (International PCOS guideline 2023, Section Summary of key recommendations).
Measure total and free testosterone if there is no clear hirsutism; do not rely on acne or hair loss alone (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.2.5 and Recommendation 1.3.2).

Use either ultrasound or anti-Müllerian hormone for polycystic ovarian morphology, only if cycles or androgens do not already give two criteria (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.4.9 and Recommendation 1.5.5).
In adolescents who do not fully meet criteria, record 'at increased risk' and reassess by 8 years after menarche (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.1.4).

clinicalManagement.title: Screen for metabolic and other risks
actions: Arrange a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test and repeat glycaemic assessment every 1 to 3 years (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.9.3 and Recommendation 1.9.9).
Check lipids, blood pressure and weight; ask about snoring and daytime sleepiness and screen for sleep apnoea (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.10.2).
Screen for depression, anxiety and eating disorders using validated tools (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 2.2.1, Recommendation 2.2.2 and Recommendation 2.5.1).
Inform the woman of a higher risk of endometrial hyperplasia; routine endometrial screening is not recommended (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.11.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Start lifestyle management
actions: Recommend healthy eating, regular physical activity and behavioural support to every woman, co-designed with her and without weight stigma (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 3.1.1, Recommendation 3.1.2 and Recommendation 3.1.4).

clinicalManagement.title: Choose medicines with shared decision-making
actions: Tell the woman that medicines are used off-label (International PCOS guideline 2023, Section Pharmacology treatment principles).

For irregular cycles and hirsutism offer a combined oral contraceptive pill; metformin where the pill is not suitable or for metabolic aims (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.2.1, Recommendation 4.4.2 and Recommendation 4.4.5).
If hirsutism has not improved after at least 6 months of the pill or cosmetic treatment, add an anti-androgen with reliable contraception (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.6.1).
For infertility from anovulation, letrozole is first-line when there are no other infertility factors; refer to fertility care (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 5.3.1).
Consider laser or light hair removal for facial hirsutism (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.8.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Follow up
actions: Review at least yearly for symptoms, weight, blood pressure and mood; repeat glucose testing every 1 to 3 years (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.9.3).

In pregnancy planning, offer the glucose test and optimise weight, blood pressure and folate; in pregnancy, offer the glucose test at the first antenatal visit and at 24 to 28 weeks (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.10.7 and Recommendation 5.1.2).

regimens.indication: Management of irregular menstrual cycles and hirsutism in polycystic ovary syndrome
regimens.patientGroup: Reproductive-age women and adolescents with polycystic ovary syndrome, not planning pregnancy
regimens.genericName: Drospirenone 3 mg and ethinyl estradiol 0.03 mg (combined oral contraceptive pill)
regimens.dose: One yellow active tablet daily for 21 days followed by one white inactive tablet daily on days 22 to 28, then start the next pack (Yasmin label, Dosage and Administration 2.1 and 2.2). Each active tablet contains 3 mg drospirenone and 0.03 mg ethinyl estradiol (Yasmin label, Description). Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablet.
regimens.route: Oral, at the same time every day, preferably after the evening meal or at bedtime with some liquid; can be taken without regard to meals (Yasmin label, Dosage and Administration 2.2)
regimens.duration: Ongoing while needed; review benefit and risks regularly. Start on day 1 of the period; if started later, use a back-up non-hormonal method for 7 days (Yasmin label, Dosage and Administration 2.2)
adjustments: Use in polycystic ovary syndrome is off-label: the guideline says medical therapy is generally not approved specifically for polycystic ovary syndrome, so tell the patient and discuss evidence and side effects (International PCOS guideline 2023, Section Pharmacology treatment principles).

The guideline recommends no specific pill, so general population contraceptive guidance applies when choosing the type; 30 microgram or lower ethinylestradiol is as good as higher doses for hirsutism (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.2.3 and Recommendation 4.2.4).
Ethinylestradiol 35 microgram with cyproterone acetate is second-line because of venous thromboembolism risk (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.2.5).

Drospirenone has anti-mineralocorticoid activity, similar to 25 mg of spironolactone, with a risk of high potassium in people with kidney, liver or adrenal problems or on potassium-sparing medicines (Yasmin label, Warnings 5.2).

Hormonal androgen tests are unreliable on the pill: stop it for at least 3 months and use another contraceptive if androgens must be measured (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.2.6).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Blood pressure at each review (Yasmin label, Warnings 5.6).
Signs of blood clots: leg pain or swelling, chest pain, sudden breathlessness, severe headache or visual loss (Yasmin label, Warnings 5.1).
Potassium in those with risk factors (Yasmin label, Warnings 5.2).
contraindications: Smoker over 35 years of age (Yasmin label, Boxed Warning and Contraindications 4).

Current or past deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism, cerebrovascular or coronary disease, inherited or acquired clotting disorder, uncontrolled hypertension, diabetes with vascular disease, migraine with aura or headaches with focal neurological symptoms (Yasmin label, Contraindications 4).
Renal impairment, adrenal insufficiency, liver tumour or liver disease (Yasmin label, Contraindications 4).
Breast cancer now or in the past, or undiagnosed abnormal uterine bleeding (Yasmin label, Contraindications 4).
regimens.useWhen: First choice for irregular cycles and hirsutism in a woman who does not need pregnancy now and has no clotting, blood pressure, liver, kidney or smoking contraindication.
regimens.sourceTitle: YASMIN (drospirenone and ethinyl estradiol) tablets: US prescribing information (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.2.1 to 4.2.7; Yasmin label, Section Dosage and Administration 2.1 and 2.2 and Section Contraindications 4

regimens.indication: Management of irregular cycles and metabolic features in polycystic ovary syndrome
regimens.patientGroup: Adults with polycystic ovary syndrome and body mass index of 25 kg/m2 or more, or women who cannot use the combined pill; adolescents for cycle regulation
regimens.dose: Start 500 mg once a day with the evening meal; increase by 500 mg every 1 to 2 weeks as tolerated (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.3.4); the extended-release label allows weekly 500 mg steps up to 2,000 mg once daily (Metformin label, Dosage and Administration 2.1). The guideline's suggested daily maximum is 2.5 g in adults and 2 g in adolescents. Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablet.
regimens.route: Oral; swallow whole with the evening meal and never crush, cut or chew the extended-release tablet (Metformin label, Dosage and Administration 2.1)
regimens.frequency: Once daily with the evening meal (extended-release)
regimens.duration: Long-term use appears safe; review the need regularly (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.3.4)
adjustments: Use in polycystic ovary syndrome is off-label: the guideline says medical therapy is generally not approved specifically for polycystic ovary syndrome, so tell the patient and discuss evidence and side effects (International PCOS guideline 2023, Section Pharmacology treatment principles).

Metformin and active lifestyle intervention have similar efficacy; low starting dose and extended-release tablets reduce stomach side effects (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.3.4).
Check kidney function before starting and regularly; do not start with estimated glomerular filtration rate of 30 to 45 and stop below 30 (Metformin label, Dosage and Administration 2.2).
Stop for iodinated contrast imaging, surgery and acute illness with dehydration as directed by the label (Metformin label, Dosage and Administration 2.3 and Warnings 5.1).
Low vitamin B12 may occur, especially with other risk factors; check B12 periodically (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.3.4; Metformin label, Warnings).

In pregnancy it does not prevent gestational diabetes or pre-eclampsia; use only for specific reasons such as preterm birth risk (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.11.1 and Recommendation 4.11.2).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate before starting and at least yearly (Metformin label, Dosage and Administration 2.2).
Stomach upset, malaise, muscle pain, fast breathing or drowsiness suggesting lactic acidosis: stop and seek care (Metformin label, Warnings 5.1).
Vitamin B12 where risk factors exist (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.3.4).
Glucose, weight and cycle pattern (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.3.1).
contraindications: Estimated glomerular filtration rate below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 (Metformin label, Contraindications 4).
Acute or chronic metabolic acidosis, including diabetic ketoacidosis (Metformin label, Contraindications 4).
regimens.useWhen: Choose when the pill is not suitable or accepted, or when metabolic aims (weight, glucose, lipids) dominate, particularly with body mass index of 25 or more.
regimens.sourceTitle: Metformin hydrochloride extended-release tablets: US prescribing information (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.3.1 to 4.3.4 and 4.4.2; Metformin label, Section Dosage and Administration 2.1 to 2.3 and Section Contraindications 4

regimens.indication: Hirsutism with a poor response after at least 6 months of the pill or cosmetic therapy
regimens.patientGroup: Women with polycystic ovary syndrome who are on effective contraception
regimens.dose: 25 to 100 mg a day (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.6.5); the label gives 25 to 100 mg a day, single or divided, for hypertension with titration at two-week intervals and no extra effect above 100 mg a day (Spironolactone label, Dosage and Administration 2.3). Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablet.
regimens.route: Oral, with or without food but consistently in relation to food (Spironolactone label, Dosage and Administration 2.1)
regimens.duration: Review response at around 6 months; hair response is slow (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.6.1)
adjustments: Use in polycystic ovary syndrome is off-label: the guideline says medical therapy is generally not approved specifically for polycystic ovary syndrome, so tell the patient and discuss evidence and side effects (International PCOS guideline 2023, Section Pharmacology treatment principles).

Use only with effective contraception; counsel about the risk of incomplete development of male genitalia in a male fetus (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.6.3 and Recommendation 4.6.4).

Spironolactone has lower risks of adverse effects than other anti-androgens; avoid cyproterone acetate at 10 mg or more (meningioma), and finasteride, flutamide and bicalutamide have liver risks (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.6.5).
Potassium can rise with kidney impairment, potassium supplements or ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (Spironolactone label, Warnings 5.1).
Do not combine with a drospirenone pill without checking potassium because both have anti-mineralocorticoid activity (Yasmin label, Warnings 5.2).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Serum potassium within 1 week of starting or increasing the dose and regularly thereafter (Spironolactone label, Warnings 5.1).
Blood pressure, dehydration and kidney function (Spironolactone label, Warnings 5.2).
Menstrual irregularity, breast tenderness (Spironolactone label, Warnings 5.4).
contraindications: Concomitant use of eplerenone (Spironolactone label, Contraindications 4).
Pregnancy or no effective contraception (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.6.3).
regimens.sourceEdition: International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 4.6.1 to 4.6.5; Spironolactone label, Section Dosage and Administration 2.1 and 2.3 and Section Contraindications 4

regimens.indication: Ovulation induction in anovulatory infertility in polycystic ovary syndrome, started by a fertility specialist
regimens.patientGroup: Women with polycystic ovary syndrome and anovulatory infertility, no other infertility factor, and no possibility of pregnancy
regimens.dose: The label dose is one 2.5 mg tablet once a day without regard to meals (Letrozole label, Dosage and Administration 2.1); the cycle start day, number of days and dose escalation for ovulation induction are not in the sources read and must follow the fertility specialist's protocol. Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablet.
regimens.route: Oral, with or without food (Letrozole label, Dosage and Administration 2.1)
regimens.frequency: Once daily on the days set by the fertility protocol
regimens.duration: Per cycle as set by the fertility protocol; refer for second-line options if there is no response (International PCOS guideline 2023, Section Summary of key recommendations)
adjustments: Use in polycystic ovary syndrome is off-label: the guideline says medical therapy is generally not approved specifically for polycystic ovary syndrome, so tell the patient and discuss evidence and side effects (International PCOS guideline 2023, Section Pharmacology treatment principles).
Letrozole is first-line pharmacological ovulation induction and is more effective than clomiphene for live birth (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 5.3.1 and Recommendation 5.4.5.1).

Do not give where there is any possibility of existing pregnancy; evidence does not show higher fetal abnormality than other agents (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 5.3.3 and Recommendation 5.4.5.2).
Before starting, consider tubal patency testing and a semen analysis (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 5.2.1).
Metformin alone is a less effective option where letrozole is not available (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 5.4.1.1).
Hepatic impairment: reduce the dose by 50% in severe dysfunction as per the label (Letrozole label, Dosage and Administration 2.5).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Pregnancy test before each cycle (Letrozole label, Contraindications 4).
Ovulation response and number of follicles by the fertility team (International PCOS guideline 2023, Section Summary of key recommendations).
Bone density if used long term (Letrozole label, Warnings 5.1).
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to letrozole or an excipient (Letrozole label, Contraindications 4).

regimens.sourceEdition: International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 5.3.1 to 5.3.3; Letrozole label, Section Dosage and Administration 2.1 and Section Contraindications 4

medicationPlan.note: All medicines are off-label for polycystic ovary syndrome: the use comes from the 2023 international guideline, and the dose, dilution, administration method and contraindications come from the product labels named in each row. Hormonal options for cycles are exclusive alternatives: give one. SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Two of three: clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism; ovulatory dysfunction (irregular cycles); polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound or raised anti-Müllerian hormone, after other causes are excluded (International PCOS guideline 2023, Section Summary of key recommendations).

1 to under 3 years after menarche: under 21 or over 45 days; from 3 years after menarche: under 21 or over 35 days or fewer than 8 cycles a year; over 90 days for any one cycle; primary amenorrhoea by 15 years (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.1.1).

Ultrasound and anti-Müllerian hormone are not used in adolescents; reassess at or before 8 years after menarche if features are present but criteria are not met (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.4.6, Recommendation 1.5.4 and Recommendation 1.1.4).
Modified Ferriman-Gallwey score of 4 to 6 or more, depending on ethnicity (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.3.5).
Assess at diagnosis with a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test; repeat every 1 to 3 years (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.9.2, Recommendation 1.9.3 and Recommendation 1.9.9).

In women with irregular cycles and hyperandrogenism, ultrasound or anti-Müllerian hormone is not required for diagnosis (International PCOS guideline 2023, Recommendation 1.4.9 and Recommendation 1.5.2).

teaching.scope: Woman or adolescent girl in a Saudi primary care or gynaecology clinic with irregular cycles, hirsutism, acne, hair loss or infertility: apply the 2023 international diagnostic criteria, exclude other causes, screen glucose, blood pressure, lipids, sleep apnoea, mood and endometrial risk, give lifestyle advice, and choose first medicines for cycle control, hirsutism and ovulation. Uses the 2023 international guideline, two Saudi survey studies and the product labels.
learningObjectives: Diagnose with two of three criteria after excluding other causes; do not use ultrasound in adolescents.
Do a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test at diagnosis and repeat every 1 to 3 years.
Offer lifestyle advice to everyone, then a combined pill or metformin; add an anti-androgen after 6 months if needed.
Use letrozole first for ovulation induction under fertility care.
pitfalls: Diagnosing from ultrasound alone or in the first year after menarche.
Measuring androgens while on the pill.
Skipping glucose testing in a thin woman.
keyPoints: All medicines are off-label and need a shared decision.
Anti-androgens and letrozole need a pregnancy test and effective contraception.
Hormone tests are unreliable on the pill.
Screen for sleep apnoea, depression and eating disorders.

patientEducation: Polycystic ovary syndrome is common and treatable; it affects periods, hair, skin, weight and fertility.
A healthy diet and regular exercise help even if you do not lose weight.
Your doctor will check your blood sugar, blood pressure and cholesterol, because the risk of diabetes is higher.
Medicines help your periods, hair growth or fertility; they are used off-label and we will talk through the choices.
If you are planning pregnancy, tell us early so we can optimise your health.
Tell us if you feel low, anxious or have trouble sleeping.
lifestyleAndDiet: Aim for regular physical activity and a balanced diet that you can keep up.
Avoid smoking, especially if you take the pill.
Laser hair removal is an option for facial hair.
Talk to a clinician about folate before pregnancy.
mdtReferrals: Primary care physician; gynaecologist; endocrinologist; dietitian; psychologist; dermatologist; fertility specialist; sleep physician where indicated.
dischargeCriteria: Diagnosis and criteria met documented; glucose test, lipids, blood pressure and mood screen recorded; lifestyle plan agreed; chosen medicine, off-label discussion and contraception plan documented; follow-up booked.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review at 3 months after starting treatment and then at least yearly; repeat glucose testing every 1 to 3 years; reassess adolescents at or before 8 years after menarche.
